messages:
mike: proposing a lightweight 'weight-catalog' service to simplify resolver logic across safetensors, tarballs, and remote shards. main goals: single source of truth for bundle layout, fast hinting for mmap vs stream, and patch/overlay awareness. thoughts?

anya: curious — is this catalog just metadata or will it own routing/fallback too?

mike: metadata-first. small hintset for runtime: {preferred_io: mmap|stream, shard_count, index_sidecar:true|false, coldstart_priority:int}. resolver may consult catalog then fall back to existing heuristics.

kyle: sounds useful. two tradeoffs to call out: 1) storing "preferred_io" centralizes ops decisions but risks staleness if instance has different hardware; 2) adding routing/fallback in catalog simplifies clients but couples catalog to infra policies.

anya: re: staleness — we could allow per-request overrides. runtime checks catalog.hints but can query local host profile to override preferred_io. e.g. GPU with NVMe and >64GB RAM => mmap preferred.

mike: agreed. catalog should be advisory. also want overlay/patched-snapshot awareness so can hot-swap small diffs without re-uploading entire bundle. manifest sketch: 
```json
{
  "bundle_id": "redwood/gptx-8b:2026-03-p0",
  "shards": ["s3://.../b00","s3://.../b01"],
  "index": "s3://.../b.idx",
  "hints": {"preferred_io":"mmap","index_sidecar":true,"hotpatch_layer":"overlays/v1/"}
}
```

kyle: hotpatch layer is nice. but how do we ensure safe warmup semantics? if overlay provides only a few tensors, warmup should prioritize base weights then overlay apply. race conditions if overlay download slower.

anya: proposal: warmup phases — phase 0: manifest resolve; phase 1: index fetch (if sidecar) + mapping; phase 2: stream critical shards (attention, embedding tables) low-latency; phase 3: background fetch remaining shards and apply overlays; phase 4: verify checksums. that lets inference start earlier.

mike: +1. also add an eviction hint to manifest for shared-host caches so we can precompute priority score per-shard. small numeric priority in manifest.

infra-bot: note — recent TTL change for shared-volume cache will reduce retention to 6h. please account for higher coldstart frequency.

kyle: given infra-bot note, catalog should expose a 'coldstart_friendly' boolean. if true, publish an optimized small warmup pack (subset payload) that contains only tensors required for <2-token latency targets.

anya: implementation note: keep catalog resolution lightweight. runtime should do a single HTTP GET to catalog and then parallel range requests to blobstore. avoid multiple RPC hops. maybe fuse index+manifest fetch when index_sidecar=true.

mike: action items: 1) prototype catalog schema + small service (mike) 2) warmup-phase API for runtime to accept 'critical_shards' list (anya) 3) overlay apply ordering and checksum PCR (kyle) 4) bench coldstart on dev cluster after infra TTL roll (infra). I'll drop a short RFC draft later today. :rocket:
